correctness.rationale: For Shrikhande Cayley graph on Z4² with 6 specified steps, the Alexander dual K consists of subsets containing no disconnected induced triple. Its graph has 48 edges, 32 triangles, each neighborhood is C6, and every pair has two common neighbors. Counting connected triples, 48 diamond and 12 four-cycle tetrahedra gives f(K)=(16,120,176,60), no 5-faces. Every tetrahedron has a globally free path triple; sixty elementary collapses leave 2D. Clique complex is the triangular 4x4 torus; each nonclique K edge is homotopic via a filled triangle to a clique path, so pi1(torus) surjects to pi1(K); coordinate 4-cycles bound K tetrahedra, killing both Z² generators. Thus K simply connected, reduced H2 free of rank chi-1=11, K≃vee_11 S² via Hurewicz and Whitehead. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality gives only H_tilde11(Delta;Z)=Z^11, other degrees zero, nonshellable as facets dimension12. Independently enumerated exact f-vector and incidence, Euler 12 and boundary ranks (15,105,60) mod 2,3,5,7; field ranks alone cannot rule out integral torsion, structural argument does.

value.rationale: The canonical Shrikhande and 4x4 rook strongly regular graphs share (16,6,2,2) and spectrum. Their ordinary three-cut integral homology ranks 11 and 27 differ, producing a structural topological discriminator. The dual wedge-of-spheres proof and non-shellability add interpretation beyond a single computed rank.
